operators.name: sum_dim1_keepdim

parameters.name: x
parameters.shape: same as input: [batch, channels, depth, height, width]

returns.shape: same as input but with channel dimension reduced to 1: [batch, 1, depth, height, width]

semantics: Computes torch.sum(x, dim=1, keepdim=True)
Reduction over dimension 1 (channel axis) preserving the dimension as size 1
Output element [b,0,d,h,w] = sum_{c} x[b,c,d,h,w]
No bias, no broadcasting beyond the reduction
Input and output are CUDA float32 tensors with same batch, depth, height, width

operators.name: maxpool3d

parameters.name: x
parameters.shape: any 5D tensor: [batch, channels, depth, height, width]

returns.shape: output shape determined by maxpool: [batch, channels, floor((depth - kernel_size)/stride)+1, floor((height - kernel_size)/stride)+1, floor((width - kernel_size)/stride)+1]

semantics: Computes 3D max pooling as nn.MaxPool3d(kernel_size, stride=stride, padding=0, dilation=1, ceil_mode=False)
The pool window is kernel_size triple; the stride is stride triple
Output element is the maximum value in the corresponding input window
Input and output are CUDA float32 tensors
No padding, dilation 1, no ceil mode
Channel-wise sum with keepdim=True
Reduction over dimension 1
Output shape [4,1,512,256,256] for given input
CUDA float32 tensor
3D max pooling with kernel_size=(2,2,2), stride=(2,2,2), padding=0, dilation=1, ceil_mode=False
Output shape [4,1,256,128,128] for given input
CUDA float32 tensor
Final output is the pooled tensor
Same as step_002
CUDA float32 tensor
